rules.quote: Include the main words and phrases that people search for.
rules.specification: Assessment requires evidence of the audience's main search terms. The page does not identify those terms or define which terms count as main.
rules.violation_condition: Content omits the main search words or phrases used by its intended audience.
rules.why: G-5: this specifies a property of the content, unlike the preceding instruction to conduct research.

rules.specification: Interpret clarity as allowing a user encountering the title in search results or through a screen reader to understand the page's subject.
rules.violation_condition: A page title does not clearly communicate what the page is about.
rules.why: G-4: the first sentence states the rule; the following sentence explains its importance.

rules.quote: Organise content in a clear order using section headings.
rules.specification: Assess whether section headings organise the content into an understandable sequence. The page does not prescribe a particular sequence or heading scheme.
rules.violation_condition: The content lacks a clear organisation expressed through section headings.
rules.why: G-2: section headings and clear ordering form one content-organisation requirement.

rules.quote: Write link text that makes the destination and purpose of the link clear.
rules.specification: Assess whether the link wording communicates where the link leads and what following it is for. The sentence does not prescribe particular wording.
rules.violation_condition: Link text leaves the link's destination or purpose unclear.
rules.why: G-2: destination and purpose are combined aspects of the link-text requirement.

rules.quote: Write clear and concise headings to help users find the information they're looking for.
rules.specification: Assess clarity and concision in relation to the content introduced by the heading. No numerical length limit is stated.
rules.violation_condition: A heading is unclear or unnecessarily wordy, making the information it introduces difficult to locate.
rules.why: G-2: clarity and concision jointly describe the heading's effectiveness as a finding aid.
